title: Why do the leaves fall?
lines: Lotte goes for a walk in the park with Grandpa.
Lotte is wearing her yellow raincoat and her red boots.
Grandpa has a warm scarf on.
In summer all the leaves were green.
But now you can see red, orange, yellow and brown.
Why do the leaves change colour?
In summer the tree makes food with its leaves.
That's why the leaves are green.
Then the tree stops making food.
And then you can see the other lovely colours.
A breeze blows through the park.
Lots and lots of leaves fall down.
But why do they fall, Grandpa?
There's not much water for the tree.
The tree can't keep all its leaves.
That way the tree saves its strength.
It goes to sleep for a while until spring.
There are little bumps on the branch.
In spring new leaves will come out of them.
She kicks a big pile of leaves.
The squirrel has a nut in its mouth.
It digs a little hole and puts the nut in the ground.
It's making a store for the winter, says Grandpa.
In winter it won't find much food.
Then it digs the nuts up again.
Under a bush Lotte sees another animal.
The hedgehog pushes its nose into the leaves.
It's looking for a warm spot.
The hedgehog is going to have a long winter sleep, says Grandpa.
Under a thick blanket of leaves.
It won't wake up again until spring.
High in the sky a long line of birds is flying.
On the ground Lotte sees something funny too.
A red one with white spots.
We only look with our eyes.
Lotte picks up a few more things.
An acorn with a little hat.
At home Grandma makes hot chocolate.
Lotte puts all her treasures on the table.
She sticks the leaves onto a big piece of paper.
She makes a little man out of the conker and the acorn.
The leaves turn red and yellow.
They fall because the tree is going to rest.
And the geese fly to the warm south.
The tree in the garden looks a bit bare.
